title: Polaris Fulfillment — Returns Assistant kickoff scratchbook
body:
Context:
Quick scratch for the kickoff with Polaris Fulfillment (3/02 call). They're building an automated returns assistant to streamline RMA and routing decisions across 4 warehouse regions (NA/EU/APAC + edge kiosks). Pilot scope: triage incoming return requests (text/photo), propose return method (label, dropoff, courier), and produce structured RMA payload for their ERP. Goal is: reduce manual review by 45% first 3 months.

Participants (call 2026-03-02):
- Devon Patel (Redwood SE)
- Maya Lin (Redwood Solutions)
- Oscar Ruiz (Polaris Eng - integration lead)
- Priya Nair (Polaris Ops)
- Samir Khatri (Polaris Security)

High-level asks from Polaris:
- On-device/edge inference for kiosks in warehouses (intermittent connectivity)
- Private deployment inside Polaris VPC for PII (order ids, customer emails)
- Low-latency decisions (<200ms median for text-only flows) for in-store kiosks
- Support for image attachments (phone photos of damage) with a small vision model + text fusion
- Structured output: JSON schema for RMA with confidence scores and fallback reasons
- Retries/fallback to manual queue; autosubmit to ERP when confidence > 0.85

Notes / gotchas from the call (raw):
- Kiosk hardware: Jetson-like devices with 8GB, intermittent connectivity to central VPC via site NAT. They prefer models that can run quantized and fit in 6GB ram on-device.
- Image quality will vary: low-light, motion blur. They want a short checklist to reject for photos that need re-upload.
- Licensing constraint: Polaris cannot send images to hosted third-party inference (privacy/legal). Private deploy only for image+text flows.
- ERP expects RMA payload posted to an internal API that accepts a specific enum set for return_reason and a 12-char order_token. We need to map model outputs to their enums reliably.
- Edge caching: kiosks will prefetch common SKU prefix info during off-peak to reduce inference context sizes. Suggest Redwood prefix/KV-cache usage.
- Throughput: 4 kiosks per site, 30 sites initially. Peak concurrency estimate 120 requests / minute with occasional burst 300/min during returns season.
- Ops: Polaris wants alerting on model drift (label distribution change) and a simple way to re-eval prompt sets. They asked about Redwood Optimize recommendations.

Technical constraints / proposed approach:
1) Deployment topology:
   - Kiosk-level: tiny local model (quantized 4-bit) for rapid triage (text-only flows + basic image heuristics). Local model should handle intent classification, slot extraction (order id, SKU), and photo-quality checks.
   - Regional/private: private Redwood cluster in Polaris VPC for “heavy” flows (image+text fusion, high-confidence structured extraction) and fallback for kiosks when connectivity is good.
   - Dedicated backup: reserved Dedicated capacity for peak days if private cluster needs burst headroom.

2) Model choices / config:
   - Local model: smaller open LLM (6–7B) quantized, optimized for on-device latency and small KV cache footprint. Consider Llama-3 micro or similar; measure tokenization cost per typical message (avg 60 tokens).
   - Regional model: larger 13–33B variant (quantized where possible) for better extraction/QA. Use Redwood routing policy to route by capability and latency.
   - Vision: small CNN/ViT-on-edge for photo heuristics (blur, lighting), URIs for images stored in S3-like object store inside VPC; heavy image classification runs in regional cluster.

3) Prompts & structured output:
   - Use strict output schema with explicit enumerated mapping (we will ship a deterministic postprocess). Example: {rma_decision: [label|dropoff|courier|manual], reason_code: <ENUM>, confidence: float, predicted_order_token: string (masked) }
   - Add function-calling style or JSON-schema enforcement on regional flows so we reduce parsing errors.

4) Batching & latency strategy:
   - Kiosks: no batching; single-request low-latency path. Keep request short.
   - Regional: continuous batching (Redwood runtime) for asynchronous bulk processing (returns scanned in batch overnight) and for reranking/QA tasks. Ensure SLOs for synchronous calls when kiosk uplinks hand off.

5) Security & privacy:
   - Data residency: images and order ids must remain in Polaris VPC. Use Redwood Private with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM).
   - Audit: Polaris needs immutable logs for decisions for 90 days. Confirm Redwood Console log retention & export options.

Open questions / followups (assign owners):
- Q1 (Oscar): Are kiosks able to run a local model update pipeline (OTA) or do images only sync upstream? Do they have TPM/hardening? (ticket INF-4296)
- Q2 (Samir): Clarify encryption/TLS termination preferences for site NAT to regional cluster + whether mutual TLS is required.
- Q3 (Priya/Oscar): Provide exact ERP enum list for return_reason and sample 50 RMA payloads (sanitized) so we can map labels.
- Q4 (Maya/Devon): Benchmark target for local quantized model on representative kiosk (we need log files + sample payloads).
- Q5 (Devon): Confirm seasonal peak forecast for capacity planning (Polaris ops to share last 2 years returns spikes).

Immediate next steps (rough timeline):
- 3/03: SE team to send a short onboarding checklist for kiosk spec + sample payload format (Devon) -> send to Oscar + Priya.
- 3/06: Polaris to upload sample 50 sanitized RMAs + list of return_reason enums to Confluence page (Oscar).
- 3/09: Prototype plan review: local model candidate + regional model candidate + estimated mem/latency numbers (Maya/Devon).
- 3/16: Onsite kiosk hardware snapshot & initial local benchmark run (if dev kits available).

Decision notes / heuristics to lock later:
- Confidence threshold for autosubmission: start at 0.85, but include conservative fallback to manual queue for items that touch high-value SKUs or flagged by ops.
- Photo rejection heuristics: reject when blur_score > 0.6 or detected occlusion on barcode area. Need to prototype simple CV heuristics before full model.

Loose ideas worth exploring:
- Client-side (kiosk) small image compressor + local blur/lighting check to avoid sending noisy photos to regional cluster and reduce bandwidth.
- Use prefix caching on SKU metadata in kiosks so prompts include minimal context (reduce tokens).
- Auto-generated short explain text for operations to speed human review queue: 1–2 sentence rationale with highlight of conflicting signals.

Risks:
- If kiosk hardware cannot support the local model size, we'll need to shift dependency to the regional cluster -> increases latency and network costs.
- Mapping model outputs to rigid ERP enums may require rule-based post-processing and human-in-loop tuning.

Logs / artifacts to attach (placeholders):
- polaris/kiosk-hw-spec-2026-02.csv (they will upload)
- polaris/sample-rma-50.json (sanitized)

End of scratch. This doc is informal — will iterate after Polaris drops artifacts. Keep this as working capture; move formal plan into Confluence once we have enums + sample payloads.

Quick TODO (Devon): email Oscar + Priya with onboarding checklist, link to INF-4296, cc Maya.
